knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Clearing the path first moves debris away from cleaned areas. Starting ease (option 0) and fuel life (option 2) are not the reason.
Debris is collected and placed in the designated waste container, and fire exits are kept clear. Leaving piles (option 0) and blowing into a neighbour's yard (option 2) are not acceptable.
Eye and hearing protection, both hands on the blower, and no smoking nearby are the controls. Sunglasses only (option 1) and optional hearing protection (option 2) do not meet the controls.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied paved area with leaves, the learner clears large objects, surveys the area and sets the nozzle direction before starting the blower; the assessor observes the set-up before the first run.
The learner clears a path down the middle first, then blows debris away from cleaned sections on alternating sides; the assessor checks no cleaned section is re-contaminated.

The learner wears eye and hearing protection throughout, keeps both hands on the blower, and gathers the piled debris with a dustpan and banister brush into the waste container; the assessor observes each item.
The learner leaves the fire-exit path clear and records the area as completed, using a supplied record sheet.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Area record for the observed task
Photo of the cleared exit path, where the site permits
stopWorkCriteria: Learner runs the blower without eye or hearing protection
Learner blows debris toward people, vehicles, a neighbour's property or back across a cleaned area
Learner smokes or refuels the blower near a flame or while it is running
Learner leaves debris blocking a fire exit or stairwell path at handover
